topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students to the final lecture and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional treatments: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles and limitations of traditional cancer interventions, detailing the mechanisms, systemic toxicity, and resistance problems of cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies that exploit inherent biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted therapies and kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, design, and clinical resistance mechanisms associated with therapies targeting specific oncogenic drivers and hyperactive kinases.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are engineered to target tumor cell-surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of immune surveillance in cancer and detail therapeutic strategies that harness, reactivate, or genetically engineer T cells to eliminate tumors.

topics.label: Challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate systemic challenges, historical improvements in survival, future strategies, and the clinical dilemmas surrounding novel versus traditional cancer treatments.
